descriptor: Matching set on pollutants: identify the heavy metal formerly blended into US gasoline to raise octane.
solution: Tetraethyl lead was added to gasoline for decades to prevent engine knock, and exhaust spread lead widely until leaded fuel was phased out. Lead is the metal that matches. Radon is a gas, mercury is tied to coal burning and fish, and copper and iron were never fuel additives.

descriptor: Same pollutant list: which is the radioactive gas that seeps from uranium-bearing rock?
solution: Radon-222 forms when uranium decays in rock and soil and is a colorless gas that can move up into buildings. None of the metals listed are gases at ordinary temperatures, so radon is the only fit.

descriptor: Same pollutant list: which is the leading cause of lung cancer in the US among these (after smoking)?
solution: Radon that collects in basements and poorly ventilated rooms is inhaled, and its radioactive decay products damage lung tissue. It is the largest source of lung cancer among non-smokers. The listed metals harm other organs, such as the nervous system, rather than being the main cause of lung cancer.
notes: Item as printed asks for a leading cause among the listed choices.

descriptor: Same pollutant list: which metal makes large predatory ocean fish a health risk for people who eat them often?
solution: Mercury, released mostly from coal burning, deposits in water, is converted to methylmercury and biomagnifies up the food chain. Top predators such as swordfish and tuna carry the highest concentrations, so heavy consumers risk neurological damage.

descriptor: World map with five marked regions: pick the region holding vast methane hydrate stores that would speed warming if released.
solution: Large deposits of methane trapped in ice-like hydrates lie in cold Arctic permafrost and shallow Arctic seabed. Warming can free this methane, a potent greenhouse gas, adding to further warming. The keyed region is the high-latitude one in the northwest of the map (Alaska/Arctic).
notes: Methane hydrates themselves are not named in the 2026 CED, though Arctic permafrost methane feedback is covered under Topic 9.5. Figure (world map) read: D marks Alaska/Arctic.

descriptor: Same world map: which region is warming fastest on average because of human-caused climate change?
solution: The Arctic warms roughly two to three times faster than the global average because loss of reflective ice and snow exposes darker surfaces that absorb more sunlight. The keyed region is the Arctic one in the northwest of the map.

descriptor: Same world map: where do destructive tornadoes occur most often?
solution: Tornadoes are most frequent over the central United States, where warm moist air from the Gulf of Mexico meets cool dry air from the north and west over flat land. The keyed region is the one over the central US.
notes: Tornado climatology is not in the 2026 CED.

descriptor: Same world map: where is tropical forest fragmentation by people driving major biodiversity loss?
solution: Tropical forests of central Africa (the Congo basin) are being cut into isolated patches by logging, farming and roads. Smaller fragments hold fewer species and expose edges to disturbance, so biodiversity falls. The keyed region is the equatorial African one.
notes: Map position of B (equatorial central Africa) read from figure.

descriptor: Same world map: which region has been the world's largest petroleum exporter for roughly forty years?
solution: The Middle East holds the largest concentration of proven oil reserves and has led global petroleum exports for decades. The keyed region is the one over the Arabian Peninsula and Persian Gulf area.

descriptor: World plate map with five lettered locations: which shows chains of volcanic islands formed above subducting plates?
solution: Island arcs form where oceanic plate descends beneath another oceanic plate and the melting produces curved chains of volcanoes. The keyed location lies in the western Pacific, a classic subduction setting.

descriptor: Same plate map: which location has a rising non-volcanic mountain range from continental collision?
solution: When two continental plates collide neither subducts easily, so crust crumples and thickens, building mountains such as the Himalayas without volcanoes. The keyed location is on the India–Eurasia boundary.

descriptor: Same plate map: where is new crust forming at a divergent boundary?
solution: At divergent boundaries plates pull apart and magma rises to make new crust. The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is the clearest example on the map, and the keyed location sits along it.

descriptor: Five climatographs (monthly precipitation and temperature): choose the climate supporting the greatest tree-species diversity.
solution: Tropical rainforest has constant warmth near 25–30 °C and heavy rain every month, giving the highest productivity and the most tree species. The keyed graph shows flat high temperature with large precipitation in all months.

descriptor: Same climatographs: which climate favors dry scrub with frequent fires?
solution: Chaparral, the shrubland of Mediterranean-type climates, has mild wet winters and hot dry summers; dry summer vegetation burns often. The keyed graph shows rain concentrated in winter months and almost none in summer.

descriptor: Table of five countries with fertility, infant mortality and life expectancy: which is most likely shrinking in population?
solution: Replacement-level fertility is about 2.1 births per woman. The keyed country has a fertility rate below that (1.8) while having long life expectancy, so deaths will eventually exceed births without immigration. Countries at or above 2.1 will not shrink.

descriptor: Same table: which country most likely offers women limited education?
solution: High fertility (6.5), very high infant mortality and low life expectancy together are typical where women have little schooling and few options, since education lowers fertility and child deaths. The keyed country shows the most extreme values on all three.

descriptor: Which process is NOT powered by the Sun: plant growth, ocean currents, hurricanes, plate tectonics, or cloud formation?
solution: Solar energy drives photosynthesis, winds and ocean circulation, storms and evaporation that forms clouds. Plate tectonics is driven by heat from Earth's interior and mantle convection, so it is the exception.

descriptor: Why are phytoplankton concentrated in the upper few hundred feet of water?
solution: Phytoplankton photosynthesize, so they must stay in the sunlit (photic) zone; light fades quickly with depth. Hiding from predators, being benthic, or eating zooplankton do not explain their position since they are producers floating in the water column.

descriptor: Which pair of exhaust pollutants do catalytic converters reduce?
solution: A catalytic converter uses metal catalysts to turn carbon monoxide and unburned hydrocarbons into CO₂ and water (and also to convert NOₓ to N₂). It does not remove CO₂, lead, mercury or particulates, so the pair CO and hydrocarbons is correct.

descriptor: Which statement correctly describes how a fuel cell vehicle works?
solution: A hydrogen fuel cell combines hydrogen with oxygen electrochemically, producing electricity and water; the electricity runs the motor. The other descriptions fit hybrids, biodiesel, solar cells or steam turbines instead.

descriptor: Which graph shows soil organic matter falling over time under long-term cropping without manure or fertilizer?
solution: Continuous cultivation removes plant material and speeds decomposition, so with no organic inputs the soil organic matter declines. The keyed graph shows a downward trend, not a rise or a flat line.
notes: Graph options (A–E) not individually described; key C taken from official key and consistent with a declining trend.

descriptor: Soil texture triangle: read the sand, silt and clay percentages at marked point T.
solution: Reading along the three triangle axes, point T sits at about 10 % clay, 30 % silt, and the remaining 60 % is sand. Percentages must total 100, which also rules out other rows.

descriptor: Same triangle: which point's texture best suits lining a landfill?
solution: A landfill liner must block leachate, so a clay-rich soil with tiny, tightly packed particles and very low permeability is best. Point W is the one with the highest clay percentage.

descriptor: Diagram of warm air over a layer of cold air trapping pollution over a town: name the phenomenon.
solution: A thermal inversion occurs when a warm layer sits above cooler air, stopping the cooler air from rising so pollutants stay near the ground in a shallow mixing depth. Albedo, greenhouse effect and heat islands do not describe this layering.

descriptor: Which statement about the Ogallala Aquifer is correct?
solution: The Ogallala lies beneath the US Great Plains (High Plains) and supplies irrigation water there; withdrawals far exceed its slow recharge, so it is being depleted. The other options place it on the wrong continents or in the wrong region.

descriptor: How will warming over 200 years probably alter the range of red pine, now limited to cool northern areas?
solution: As climate warms, suitable habitat for cold-adapted species shifts poleward and uphill. Red pine's range should therefore move northward into Canada, while southern areas become too warm.

descriptor: Which sequence is a positive feedback loop in the Arctic under climate change?
solution: A positive feedback amplifies the original change: melting ice exposes darker water that absorbs more sunlight, warming the surface, which melts more ice. Only the choice in which melting leads to warmer water and more melting shows this reinforcement.

descriptor: Before a solar plant is built, what baseline data would let a student test whether panel shade raises creosote bush mortality?
solution: Shade affects plants by reducing the light they receive, so measuring the direct sunlight reaching creosote bushes before construction gives the baseline to compare with after shading. Noise, global CO₂, erosion and rain are not the variable in the hypothesis.

descriptor: Succession graph of tree biomass after clear-cutting: at which time is species richness highest?
solution: Species richness is highest when the greatest number of species are present at once. Around 100 years the pioneer sweet gum is still declining while oak, hickory, beech and dogwood have all established, so most species overlap then.
notes: Read from graph; five curves compared.

descriptor: Same graph: which tree does best in full sun?
solution: Sweet gum rises first and peaks early, then disappears as the canopy closes, showing it is a pioneer needing full sunlight. Later species such as beech and dogwood tolerate shade.

descriptor: Why are most deserts near 30° north and south latitude?
solution: In the Hadley cell warm air rises at the equator and drops moisture as rain, then flows poleward, cools and sinks near 30°. Sinking air warms and dries, giving low humidity and desert conditions.

descriptor: Which item is NOT household hazardous waste: batteries, bug spray, motor oil, oil-based paint, or food scraps?
solution: Household hazardous wastes contain toxic, flammable or corrosive substances and need special disposal. Food scraps are organic and can be composted or landfilled, so they are the exception.

descriptor: Why does a hybrid electric vehicle use less fuel per mile than an ordinary car?
solution: Regenerative braking turns the car's kinetic energy into electricity stored in the battery, which later helps drive the motor. This recaptures energy that conventional brakes waste as heat. Hybrids still burn gasoline and are not solar powered.

descriptor: Why do small isolated islands lose species at higher rates than large near islands?
solution: Island biogeography predicts that small islands support fewer resources and fewer niches, so populations are small and vulnerable. Isolation also reduces recolonization, so extinction outpaces immigration.

descriptor: On a growth graph, what does the horizontal line labeled K show?
solution: K is the carrying capacity: the maximum population size the environment can sustain indefinitely given limiting resources. A logistic growth curve levels off at K.

descriptor: Which of five diagrams correctly shows the nitrogen cycle?
solution: The correct cycle has atmospheric N₂ fixed into ammonium, nitrified to nitrite and then nitrate, taken up by plants, and returned to the air as N₂ by denitrification. The keyed diagram follows that order; the others have impossible conversions.

descriptor: Graph of glyphosate use and herbicide-resistant weed species both rising: which statement explains it?
solution: Heavy repeated spraying kills susceptible weeds but leaves resistant individuals that reproduce, so resistance spreads. This is natural selection, and explains why the count of resistant weeds climbs with usage.

descriptor: Which is a concern about growing more genetically modified crops?
solution: Planting a few uniform GM varieties widely can narrow the genetic diversity of crops, making them more vulnerable to pests or disease. The other options are false claims about yield or soil limits.

descriptor: How might agricultural herbicide runoff contribute to amphibian declines?
solution: Some herbicides mimic or interfere with hormones; as endocrine disruptors they can alter amphibian development and reproduction. The thin permeable skin of amphibians makes them especially sensitive.

descriptor: Graph of US electricity sources 1950–2010: pick the most valid inference.
solution: The data show coal generation falling around 2008 as natural gas and renewables grew; this competition is the supported explanation. The other options attribute trends to causes (shortages, costs, laws) that the graph cannot show.

descriptor: Five age-structure diagrams: which population most likely has a negative growth rate?
solution: A pyramid-shaped diagram signals future growth, a straight-sided column signals stability, and a top-heavy shape with a narrow base signals decline. Diagram D alone has more people in older age groups than in the youngest, so deaths and aging will outweigh births.

descriptor: Table of stream measurements: which site is likely just downstream of construction?
solution: Compare each site with the unaffected reference sites (B and D), which have clear water and low solids. Rain on bare construction soil also carries sediment but not acid, so pH stays near neutral, unlike the acidified Site E (pH 4.0).

descriptor: Corn needs 1 ha per 1,000 kcal; beef takes 20 times more land: which equation gives land for 10,000 kcal of beef?
solution: Land per kcal of corn is 1 ha/1,000 kcal; each kcal of beef requires 20 kcal of corn. Multiplying 1 ha/1,000 kcal by 20 kcal corn per kcal beef by 10,000 kcal beef gives 200 ha, and the units cancel correctly.

descriptor: Which is an advantage of nuclear power for electricity?
solution: Compared with coal, nuclear fission produces no CO₂ at the plant. Waste storage, accident risk, high capital cost and warm-water discharge are its drawbacks, which is why the other options are wrong.

descriptor: Which soil component most likely neutralizes acid rain?
solution: Acid rain is neutralized by bases, and carbonate rock is the common natural buffer. Soils over limestone resist acidification, whereas soils over granite are poorly buffered and lakes in those areas acidify.

descriptor: Besides birth control access, what else is a likely cause of the projected decline in world growth rate?
solution: Rising female employment and education typically delay marriage and reduce the number of children per woman, so the growth rate falls. Fewer pandemics, more births in developed nations or longer lifespans would push growth up, not down.

descriptor: How does El Niño cause a drop in southern California brown pelican numbers?
solution: Fish-eating birds depend on a steady fish supply near their nests. When warm El Niño water reduces fish near the coast, adults cannot find enough food for chicks, and breeding success and numbers fall.

descriptor: Why does the open ocean contain the largest share of Earth's producer biomass?
solution: Per unit area, open-ocean productivity is low, but because the ocean is so large the sum of producers (mostly microscopic phytoplankton) is larger than on any other ecosystem type. Size, not individual producer size, drives the total.

descriptor: Diagram of gases over a city on a smoggy day: which explains the pattern in NO concentration?
solution: Nitric oxide is emitted directly (primary pollutant) by engines, so it rises with morning traffic. It is then oxidized to NO₂ and consumed in smog chemistry, so its concentration falls through the day.
notes: Graph (gas concentration versus time of day) not individually inspected; key D from official key and consistent with standard smog chemistry.

descriptor: If hydrocarbon emissions were reduced, what would most likely happen to smog constituents?
solution: Hydrocarbons (VOCs) and NOₓ react in sunlight to form ozone, so removing a reactant cuts ozone production. NO would not rise because it is not produced from hydrocarbons, and CO₂ is not tied to this change.

descriptor: Table of five reclaimed mine sites: choose the one with the best forest reclamation after ten years.
solution: Compare indicators of the goal (a forest). Site 5 has 65 % tree cover, the fastest growth (20 cm/yr) and the least grass, meaning trees are outcompeting the seeded grass. Site 1 has mostly grass and little tree cover.
notes: Species survival tie (3 vs 4) judged less important than cover and growth.

descriptor: New suburban housing replaces farms: what is its biggest effect on the local water supply?
solution: Pavement and roofs keep water from soaking into the ground, so aquifers receive less recharge. Runoff to streams actually increases, and impervious surfaces increase, rather than decrease, erosion in streams.

descriptor: Storm runoff from the new development into a creek likely causes what?
solution: Runoff from roofs, roads and construction carries sediment and suspended solids that cloud the water and bury spawning beds. Mercury biomagnification, malaria, and ozone as a drinking-water contaminant are unrelated to storm runoff.

descriptor: Which homeowner step would help protect creek water quality?
solution: Rain barrels hold roof runoff so less flows quickly to the creek, reducing flooding, erosion and pollutant loads. Fertilizer before a storm and pet waste in drains add nutrients and pathogens, and channelizing speeds flow and worsens erosion.

descriptor: Beak sizes of finches on two islands differ although the species is the same: choose the best hypothesis.
solution: Because the birds are one species and beak size is genetic, a consistent difference points to natural selection by different food on each island, such as seeds of different hardness. Distance of ten kilometers does not explain the pattern with movement, since the birds would mix.

descriptor: A family of five switches from 5 to 2 gallons-per-minute showerheads (8 min each daily): water saved in 30 days?
solution: Savings per minute: 5 − 2 = 3 gal. Total shower time: 5 people × 8 min × 30 days = 1,200 min. Water saved: 3 gal/min × 1,200 min = 3,600 gallons.

descriptor: What is hydraulic fracturing used to do?
solution: Fracturing makes cracks in tight rock formations and the sand props them open so trapped hydrocarbons flow to the well. It does not pulverize rock, reopen mines, cause intended earthquakes or scrub rock by abrasion.

descriptor: Which describes demographic changes at the start of transition from preindustrial to industrial?
solution: In the early industrial stage of the demographic transition, improvements in sanitation, food supply and medicine reduce the death rate first, while birth rates stay high from tradition. The gap between births and deaths produces rapid growth.

descriptor: All but one are negative externalities: which is the exception?
solution: The pollination benefit of bees goes to farmers who did not pay for it, a positive externality. The other options are costs imposed on people who did not choose them, which are negative externalities.
notes: Externalities are not named in the 2026 CED, though related cost concepts appear in unit 8.

descriptor: Bar graph of land use in four watersheds: which statement is likely true?
solution: Watersheds with high residential and commercial land cover have more impervious surfaces, so runoff reaches streams quickly and flow fluctuates strongly with rainfall. Watershed IV is mainly agricultural, so more algae from nutrient runoff, not excellent quality, is likely there.

descriptor: Which equation computes income from a farm that is 40 % trees and 60 % vegetables?
solution: Each crop's income per hectare must be multiplied by the number of hectares it occupies. With total hectares times 0.4 for trees and 0.6 for vegetables, the two terms are added to give total income, so units of dollars result.

descriptor: What is the most direct result of surface ocean circulation?
solution: Surface currents driven by winds and Earth's rotation move warm water poleward and cold water toward the tropics, moderating climates. They do not cause lake turnover, restrict the jet stream or reduce ocean acidification.
notes: Surface ocean currents are touched on in 4.8/4.9; coverage is light.

descriptor: Using a decay curve of moles against time, estimate the half-life.
solution: On the decay graph, find where the amount reaches half its starting value, here 0.20 to 0.10 mol. Reading across at 0.10 mol gives about 7 seconds. Check: at 14 seconds the amount should be about 0.05 mol, which matches the plotted curve.

descriptor: Cause of recent cyanobacteria blooms in Lake Erie?
solution: Phosphorus from fertilizer and manure running off fields into Lake Erie drives eutrophication and cyanobacterial blooms that produce toxins. Warmer, not cooler, summers favor blooms, and chlorine would kill rather than feed algae.

descriptor: Which question is best for investigating why alpine meadow natives decline while invasive grasses spread?
solution: A good research question is specific and testable about a plausible mechanism. Air-pollution nitrogen fertilizing soils plausibly favors fast-growing invasive grasses, whereas wolves, shrub abundance or ozone-raised soil pH are weakly connected to alpine meadows.

descriptor: Experiment on ammonium sulfate and mung bean germination: which statements about the design are true?
solution: The independent variable is what the experimenter changes (concentration of ammonium sulfate), and the dependent variable is what is measured (seeds that fail to germinate). A proper control receives seeds without the chemical, not no seeds.

descriptor: A major limitation of photovoltaic cells?
solution: Photovoltaic cells produce electricity only when light strikes them, so output drops under clouds and stops at night. They have no moving parts and emit no CO₂ in operation, which are benefits, and they can feed the grid.

descriptor: Besides fertilizer, vehicle exhaust and industrial air pollution, a major source of nitrogen pollution?
solution: Human nitrogen sources include fertilizer, combustion (vehicle and industrial NOₓ) and sewage or animal waste entering water. Refrigeration units, trash dumping and oil spills are not major nitrogen sources.

descriptor: Compare CO₂ released by a 30 mpg and a 20 mpg car over 60,000 miles at 20 lb CO₂ per gallon.
solution: Fuel use scales with distance divided by efficiency, and CO₂ scales with gallons burned. The more efficient car saves 1,000 gallons, which is 20,000 lb of CO₂ at 20 lb/gal.

descriptor: Which policy would promote above-replacement fertility?
solution: Fertility above replacement means more than about 2.1 children per woman. Incentives such as priority housing for larger families encourage births, while promoting small families, abstinence or removing tax benefits does the opposite.

descriptor: Which statement about the 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments is true?
solution: The 1990 amendments targeted acid rain by capping total SO₂ emissions and letting plants trade allowances. The other options misstate the law: it did not regulate CO₂ or indoor air, or relax ozone or fuel economy limits.
notes: Specific provisions of the 1990 amendments (SO₂ allowance trading) are beyond what the 2026 CED lists; only Clean Air Act in general is covered.

descriptor: Postawko Creek table: which site is immediately downstream from a new dairy farm?
solution: Animal manure raises nitrates, phosphorus and fecal coliform bacteria; bacterial decomposition of the extra organic matter lowers dissolved oxygen and macroinvertebrate diversity. Site C has the highest nutrients and bacteria and the lowest oxygen and diversity.

descriptor: Most likely route for mercury into the food web?
solution: Mercury released in coal smoke falls to water, is converted to methylmercury, taken up by plankton, and magnified in fish. The other pathways describe routes that do not involve atmospheric transport into water food chains.

descriptor: Why are two soil samples dark and high in C and N while four are low?
solution: Topsoil (the A horizon) contains dark humus with high organic carbon and nitrogen. The B horizon accumulates minerals but holds little organic matter, so it is lighter and low in C and N.

descriptor: How does eutrophication kill fish?
solution: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms; when the algae die, bacteria decomposing them consume dissolved oxygen. Fish and other aerobic organisms suffocate, rather than being poisoned by pH, mercury or salt.

descriptor: What is true about utility bills for coal-fired electricity?
solution: Prices for coal-fired power cover fuel, plant and delivery costs but not the costs of illness, lost workdays and environmental damage borne by society. Distribution and marketing costs are in the bill.
notes: True-cost / externality accounting is not in the 2026 CED.

descriptor: Which is an example of a carbon sink?
solution: A sink absorbs or stores more carbon than it releases. Buried marine sediment stores carbon for long periods, whereas deforestation, burning and decomposition release CO₂, and lawn nutrient uptake is not long-term storage.

descriptor: Map of population doubling times: which statement is best supported?
solution: Doubling time is inversely related to growth rate (70 ÷ doubling time ≈ rate). India's 41–80 years is a faster rate than the 81–200 years shown for China and Australia. The map gives no data on population size, density, development or farmland.

descriptor: Which problem is fracking most likely to cause?
solution: Hydraulic fracturing injects fluids underground, and leaks, spills or poor well casings can contaminate drinking-water aquifers. Ozone depletion, eutrophication, denitrification and desertification are not typical results.

descriptor: Which test best checks whether hikers' trampling killed alpine plants?
solution: A valid test compares plants where the suspected cause (trampling) is present with similar areas where it is absent. Counting hikers or comparing hikers' traits does not measure effects on plants.

descriptor: What does a K-selected strategy produce?
solution: K-selected species live near carrying capacity, with long lives, slow maturity and few young. By investing heavily in each offspring they increase survival, unlike r-selected species that produce many unprotected young.

descriptor: 60 % of 2 kg per day is compostable: amount per person in a week?
solution: Compostable fraction is 0.60 of waste. Weekly waste per person is 2 kg/day × 7 days = 14 kg, and 0.60 × 14 kg = 8.4 kg.

descriptor: Which is NOT a likely result of Arctic warming?
solution: Sea ice already floats, so melting it does not change sea level, and flooding would not create farmland. The other four statements describe real or plausible Arctic consequences, including methane release from permafrost.

descriptor: NPP bar chart for three forest biomes: what explains the variation?
solution: Net primary productivity rises with warmth and abundant rainfall, as in rain forest compared with northern conifer forest. Longitude is a position on Earth that does not itself control plant growth.

descriptor: What would most likely reduce ground-level ozone in a city?
solution: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant made when NOₓ and VOCs react in sunlight. Reducing NOₓ lowers production, while sunny days, inversions and more VOCs raise it. CFCs destroy stratospheric ozone and do not affect ground-level ozone in this way.

descriptor: Which latitude has 24 hours of daylight on December 21?
solution: At the December solstice, the Sun is overhead near the Tropic of Capricorn, so the polar region of the south is tilted toward the Sun and receives continuous daylight south of the Antarctic Circle. Point E lies on that circle.

descriptor: Best description of bioaccumulation?
solution: Bioaccumulation is the buildup of a chemical within one organism over time because intake exceeds elimination. It differs from biomagnification, which is increase up trophic levels.

descriptor: Health impact most closely associated with atmospheric particulates?
solution: Fine particles lodge deep in the lungs and trigger inflammation and breathing problems such as asthma and bronchitis. Cataracts and melanoma are linked to UV radiation, not particulates.

descriptor: Which fact best supports a citizens' group claim that oak-hickory forest will not be harvestable in 50 years?
solution: Oak and hickory are late-successional trees; after clear-cutting, fast-growing pioneer species come first and it takes many decades or even centuries before large oaks are again present. This undermines the harvest plan.

descriptor: Best example of the tragedy of the commons?
solution: The tragedy of the commons occurs when a shared, unowned resource is overused or degraded because each user gains while costs are shared. Polluting the open Gulf waters fits; privately owned lakes are not commons.
notes: Key A is the official answer; option (A) is arguably a pollution example but is the best fit among options.

descriptor: Impact of CO₂ and volcanic stratospheric aerosols?
solution: CO₂ absorbs outgoing infrared radiation and warms the planet, while sulfate particulates in the stratosphere scatter sunlight and cool it for a few years. They have opposing effects.

descriptor: Which links a health effect to fine particulates correctly?
solution: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) from burning coal and other fuels penetrates deep into lungs causing respiratory disease. The other pairs link unrelated causes and effects, such as sewage with skin cancer.

descriptor: Why does anthropogenic water vapor not matter much for warming?
solution: Water vapor cycles quickly through evaporation and precipitation, staying only days in the atmosphere, so human additions don't accumulate. It matters mostly as a feedback to warming by other gases.

descriptor: Why will infectious diseases spread with climate change?
solution: Warming lets mosquitoes and ticks survive in latitudes and elevations that were too cold, widening disease range. Population growth is actually slowing, and rainforests are shrinking.

descriptor: Which hypothesis shows economic benefit of plant diversity in pastures?
solution: For ranchers, an economic benefit means more forage or income. Higher net primary productivity in diverse pastures supports more livestock, whereas lower infiltration or fewer birds are not benefits.

descriptor: Three bar graphs of irrigation water, money and return per liter: which statement is best?
solution: From the third graph, vegetables return $1,800 per million liters compared with $300 for livestock and pasture. Livestock uses the most water and earns the most money in total but yields the lowest return per liter.

descriptor: Which global change is expected from more atmospheric CO₂?
solution: Warming from higher CO₂ is predicted to cause loss of species in tropical ecosystems, along with more severe storms, more heat waves and earlier spring events. The other options say the opposite.

descriptor: Which statement is consistent with graphs of meat consumption and population?
solution: The top graph shows North American per-capita consumption (about 320 g/day) is higher than in the other regions. Population growth does not by itself raise per-capita consumption, so the other claims aren't supported.

descriptor: Health effect associated with thermal inversion?
solution: During inversions, pollutants including fine particulates are trapped near the surface, and breathing them irritates the respiratory system. Ozone, mold, CO₂ and pressure are not the main inversion problems.

descriptor: Which growth rate is paired with the correct doubling time?
solution: Use the rule of 70: doubling time = 70 ÷ growth rate (%). At 2 %, 35 years. Check others: 1 % gives 70 years, 3.5 % gives 20 years, 5 % gives 14 years.

descriptor: Newspaper article on white-nose syndrome devastating little brown bats: why disease rarely drives hosts extinct, threats to tiny populations, slow recovery, effects on other organisms, forest ecosystem services, and why human emerging diseases are increasing.
solution:
**(a) Why disease seldom causes extinction.** Any one valid reason: genetic variation means some individuals resist and survive to reproduce; hosts and pathogens co-evolve toward lower lethality; a pathogen that kills all hosts loses its own habitat; and deaths lower population density, so transmission slows. *(1 point: one correct explanation)*

**(b)(i) Two threats to a very small population.** Examples: hard to find mates when individuals are scarce or widely dispersed; low genetic diversity (inbreeding, a bottleneck, one disease able to hit nearly all individuals); competition for roosts or food from similar species; loss of group benefits such as shared warmth or protection; vulnerability to a disturbance such as a drought or fire. *(2 points: 1 each, first two only)*

**(b)(ii) Slow recovery.** Little brown bats have one or two pups a year, mature late and live long (long generation time), so population growth is slow even with high survival. Heavy parental care also limits number of offspring. *(1 point: one biological trait with explanation)*

**(c) Effects on other organisms.** Examples: more insects (bat prey) and more insect-borne disease or crop pests; fewer predators of bats because less food; fewer plants that bats pollinate or whose seeds they disperse; less guano feeding cave communities; less fungus (WNS) if bats are fewer; competitors with similar niches gain; trophic cascade. *(2 points: 1 each, first two only)*

**(d) Two forest ecosystem services.** Any two, each with a human benefit: timber and fuel for construction and paper; oxygen production for breathing; soil protection and water filtration giving clean drinking water and flood control; carbon sequestration slowing climate change; habitat and biodiversity supplying food, medicine; recreation and culture. *(2 points: 1 each service linked to a benefit)*

**(e) Increase in emerging human diseases.** A reason plus explanation, e.g. climate warming lets disease vectors such as mosquitoes survive in new areas; more global travel moves pathogens quickly between regions; greater contact with wildlife through habitat clearing exposes people to zoonotic pathogens; antibiotic resistance produces new strains; denser populations pass disease more easily. *(2 points: 1 reason, 1 correct explanation of how it raises disease)*
notes: Article is a newspaper-style passage with no data; all parts answered from scoring guidance concepts, restated. Ecosystem services and biodiversity map to Unit 2; disease and climate links to Units 3/9.

descriptor: Iron ore, pig iron and steel: four mass calculations from global production data and steel recycling savings, plus environmental problems of abandoned coal mines, a mitigation method, and why surface mining is cheaper.
solution:
**(a)(i) Rock waste.** Waste = ore used − pig iron produced = 1.6 × 10⁹ t − 1.2 × 10⁹ t = 0.4 × 10⁹ t = **4 × 10⁸ tons**. *(1 point: answer with work)*

**(a)(ii) Pig iron from all reserves.** Yield = 1.2 ÷ 1.6 = 0.75 t pig iron per t ore. Pig iron = 0.75 × 800 × 10⁹ t = **6.0 × 10¹¹ tons (600 billion tons)**. *(2 points: 1 for correct setup, 1 for the answer)*

**(a)(iii) Reserves going to steel.** 95 % × 800 billion t = 0.95 × 800 × 10⁹ = **7.6 × 10¹¹ tons (760 billion tons)** of iron ore. *(1 point: answer with work)*

**(b) Coal conserved.** 0.7 t coal per t steel × 80 × 10⁶ t steel = **5.6 × 10⁷ tons (56 million tons)** per year. *(1 point)*

**(c) Two problems at abandoned coal mines.** Examples: acid mine drainage and heavy-metal pollution of streams; subsidence and sinkholes from collapsed shafts; habitat destruction that recovers slowly; erosion and sediment from bare tailings; underground fires and methane release; dust. *(2 points: 1 each, first two only)*

**(d) Mitigation of one problem.** Treat acid drainage with limestone or retain runoff in ponds; replant vegetation to stop erosion; fill or seal shafts; regrade and return tailings. *(1 point: method matched to a problem named in (c))*

**(e) Surface mining cheaper.** Reason plus discussion, e.g. underground mining needs more workers, higher wages and more safety measures (ventilation, supports), and has higher costs for accidents, insurance and illness such as black lung, whereas surface mining uses large machines with fewer workers. *(2 points: reason with linked economic explanation)*
notes: Printed point total 10 (1+2+1+1+2+1+2). Part (a)(iii) reads as 95 % of the reserves, per the guideline's answer of 760 billion tons.

descriptor: Graph of US municipal solid waste 1960–2012: reason per-capita waste changed after 2000, percent increase in total MSW from 1980, drawbacks of incineration, landfills and composting, landfill-gas electricity steps, and tire-pile health problems.
solution:
**(a)(i) Cause of the change in per-capita generation, 2000–2012.** Per-capita waste fell slightly; probable causes include more recycling and reuse, lighter packaging materials (plastic in place of glass), less paper as news and magazines go online, or reduced consumption during the 2008–2009 recession. *(1 point: one cause explained)*

**(a)(ii) Percent increase in total MSW, 1980–2012.** Read from the graph: about 150 million tons in 1980 and 250 million tons in 2012. Percent increase = (250 − 150) ÷ 150 × 100 = **≈ 67 %** (66–67 % accepted). *(1 point: answer with work)*

**(b)(i) Disadvantage of incineration.** Air pollutants (CO₂, dioxins, particulates, SOₓ, NOₓ), toxic ash needing disposal, high building and operating cost, or neighbors' complaints about trucks. *(1 point)*

**(b)(ii) Disadvantage of landfills.** Leachate contaminating groundwater or soil, methane and CO₂ release, odors, vermin, habitat loss and the land they take up for decades. *(1 point)*

**(c) Electricity from landfill gas.** Step 1: methane produced by decomposing buried waste is collected through pipes. Step 2: the gas is burned, converting chemical energy to heat that makes steam (or hot gas). Step 3: the steam or hot gas turns a turbine connected to a generator, producing electricity. *(3 points: 1 per step)*

**(d) Tire piles.** Standing water in tires breeds mosquitoes that carry disease, or tire fires release smoke and toxic fumes causing respiratory problems. *(1 point)*

**(e)(i) Advantage of composting.** Produces soil amendment that can be used or sold, lowers disposal costs, less odor in trash, creates jobs. *(1 point)*

**(e)(ii) Disadvantage of composting.** Odors, attracts pests, can release methane, nutrient runoff, or requires labor and time. *(1 point)*
notes: Graph values (about 150 and 250 million tons) taken from the official guideline's calculation; the graph image itself was not examined at full resolution. Points: 1+1+1+1+3+1+1+1 = 10.

descriptor: Soil: how two climate factors affect formation rate, biotic and abiotic components of the A horizon, nitrate in groundwater from farming, acid deposition effects and remediation, and two ways climate change degrades soil.
solution:
**(a) Two climate factors and soil formation rate.** Temperature: warmth speeds weathering and microbial decomposition so soil forms faster, while cold slows biological activity (though freeze-thaw can crack rock). Precipitation: moderate to high rainfall increases weathering and biological activity; very heavy rain can erode soil and reduce formation, and very dry conditions slow it. Wind can add or remove particles. *(2 points: 1 each description, not just naming a factor)*

**(b) A horizon.** (i) Biotic: humus, roots, earthworms, fungi or bacteria. (ii) Abiotic: sand, silt, clay, water, air, minerals or nutrients. *(2 points)*

**(c)(i) Practice raising nitrates.** Heavy fertilizer application (or improperly sealed feedlots or manure lagoons). *(1 point)*

**(c)(ii) How.** Nitrate is soluble and not held by soil particles, so water percolating through the soil carries it down into groundwater (or runoff carries it to waters that recharge aquifers). *(1 point)*

**(d)(i) Effect of acid deposition on plants.** Acidic soil leaches away nutrient cations such as calcium and magnesium, releases toxic aluminum, damages roots and lowers the soil's buffering, so growth declines. *(1 point)*

**(d)(ii) Remediation.** Add crushed limestone (lime) to neutralize the acid. *(1 point)*

**(e) Two ways climate change degrades soil.** Hotter, drier conditions cause desertification; higher evaporation of irrigation water causes salinization; heavier rain increases erosion and leaching; warmer soil breaks down organic matter faster; sea level rise brings salt water to coastal soils. *(2 points: 1 each)*
notes: Points 2+2+1+1+1+1+2 = 10. Soil topics span 4.2 and 4.3, with acid deposition (7.7) and nitrate (8.5) as secondary links.
